title: Protocol loading can return an implementation from a different file
reasoning: The import identity contains only the immediate parent basename and file stem. Files such as /a/problem/main.py and /b/problem/main.py both become problem.main. After the first load, importlib returns its cached module for the second path, despite the sys.path change. This silently executes the wrong implementation when separate catalogs or snapshots reuse directory names.
reproduction: Create two distinct roots containing problem/main.py with conforming classes that return different values. Load both sequentially in one process; the second load returns the first module's class.
recommendation: Use a module/package identity derived from the resolved source location and load that exact file, preserving relative-import support without sharing cached packages across different roots.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Most tests use unique temporary-directory basenames. The nested-directory test loads only one module under its fixed basename.
suggestedRegressionTest: Extend nested loading coverage to load same-named packages from different roots sequentially, including relative dependencies, and verify each implementation and dependency comes from its requested root.
minimumFixScope: load_protocol_entrypoint import identity and protocol-loader tests.
